title: Impact of Controlled Entry and Exit Points in Buildings for SafeEntry Scanning on Fire Safety
what_it_is: Impact of Controlled Entry and Exit Points in Buildings for SafeEntry Scanning on Fire Safety

sections.label: Fire safety and cordoned exits
sections.summary: Building owners must comply with fire safety requirements, keep cordoned exits accessible, use removable barriers, display signage, and SCDF conducts enforcement checks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Building owners must continue to comply with fire safety requirements and ensure that the exits and entrances that are cordoned off must be readily accessible during emergencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: For example, the physical barriers that are used as cordons must be easily removable to allow evacuation in an emergency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Clear notices or signage must also be prominently placed to inform the public.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Singapore Civil Defence Force has communicated the fire safety requirements to all building owners and will continue to conduct regular enforcement checks to ensure compliance.

sections.label: SCDF public awareness of exits
sections.summary: SCDF has been encouraging malls and building owners to inform the public about exit use in emergencies and to place clear signage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, has SCDF considered this risk and how does it intend to mitigate that, beyond what the Minister of State mentioned just now about having signage to ensure that people are aware that the exit can actually be opened.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We recognise that it is important for us to let the public know and be socialised about how the exits and entrances work during an emergency.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: SCDF has been doing that and has been encouraging malls and building owners to inform their customers and those who go to the buildings about some of the safety aspects and, at the same time, place clear signage.

sections.label: Engaging building owners regularly
sections.summary: SCDF engages building owners regularly and will continue to manage and enhance its system and engage the public and building owners.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: As such, we have also been engaging building owners regularly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: This is something that we believe in and want to work with the public on, and while we will continue to manage and enhance our system, as well as engage the public and building owners.
